summary:
Assam stands under India's national framework, and no Assam-specific statute on gender recognition, criminal law or facilities was identified in the sources reviewed; the national assessment applies.

Assam's complaint machinery under the Transgender Persons Act has been reachable. Of the seven cases registered nationally under the Act in 2021, two were in Assam; the 2023 national tally recorded none in the state. A Queerbeat crime-data report of 30 January 2026 cautions that national counts are tiny (20 cases across 2019 to 2023) because of police-registration bias, so low counts do not indicate low incidence. The same report's 2025 survey puts prevalence of physical violence against trans people at 27.2% and sexual violence at 22.3%.

As of December 2021, Assam had not constituted a Transgender Welfare Board under the 2019 Rules; a Parliamentary reply from the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment listed 12 states and union territories that had done so, and Assam was not among them. No state welfare machinery coordinating housing, surgery or pensions therefore existed in Assam at that date.

Transgender persons arrested by the Railway Protection Force in Assam have recounted degrading treatment in custody, a state-specific instance of the police-conduct concerns documented elsewhere in India.
tangentialFactors:
Assam's raw case counts are drawn from a national total so small (20 cases across 2019 to 2023) that ranking states by these figures carries no base-rate meaning; the source itself attributes the low numbers to under-registration by police rather than to lower incidence of violence.

The absence of a Transgender Welfare Board in Assam contrasts with the twelve states and union territories that had constituted one by December 2021, several of which run housing subsidies, pensions and public-hospital surgery programmes.
localsOnly:
Residents of Assam without a state Transgender Welfare Board as of December 2021 had no state-level welfare machinery for housing subsidies, pensions or publicly funded surgery; access to such schemes would depend on national programmes and on individual district administration.

Two Transgender Persons Act complaints were registered in Assam in 2021, indicating that the statutory complaint route was usable with local police at that time, though the national reporting totals remain very small.

Transgender detainees arrested by the Railway Protection Force in Assam have reported degrading treatment in custody, a risk that falls on residents and visitors alike during arrest or detention.
outOfScopeNotes:
No Assam-specific legislation, court judgment, or state executive order on gender recognition, bathroom access, healthcare bans or partner recognition was identified in the sources reviewed; whether Assam has issued any such measure remains unresolved.

The welfare-board position is stated as of December 2021, the date of the Parliamentary reply; whether Assam constituted a board after that date is not sourced here.

The 27.2% physical and 22.3% sexual violence prevalence figures come from a 2025 survey reported by Queerbeat; the source inventory does not indicate whether these are national or Assam-specific figures, so their geographic scope is unresolved.
